recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. Do not make additional source changes for FHIR-31705 unless a new work-group decision reopens the default-tab behavior or changes the terminology navigation model.
issue_request: FHIR-31705 reported that the terminology/operations navigation skipped the 4.2 tab between Using Codes and Code Systems and asked for the default tab to become 4.1. The final R5 resolution required making the Binding examples page a distinct tab between 4.1 and 4.3, while explicitly not changing the default Terminologies tab.
initial_application: The issue was applied before this reconciliation. Commit 3e9548e1fd174e57f6b310153f25cf8f13169e0d changed source/terminologies-binding-examples.html from the default terminology header to <%txheader examples%> and adjusted heading levels so the page has its own terminology sub-tab marker. The hierarchy already included the page, and later cleanup d78907197b3fbbbafead95cc5d551aded6e3435c normalized its indentation between Using Codes and Code Systems.
additional_context: Current source/hierarchy.xml lists the Terminology module children as Using Codes, Terminology Binding Examples, Code Systems, then Value Sets. source/terminologies-binding-examples.html uses <%txheader examples%>, matching the sibling tab-marker pattern used by systems, valuesets, and service pages. publish.ini includes terminologies-binding-examples.html, confirming build scope. Jira search found no related replacement issue, Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion, and FHIR-I May 2021 minutes record the 21-0-0 Persuasive with Modification vote.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because no source edit is needed. The current build inputs already preserve the accepted tab-order change, and changing the default terminology tab would contradict the Jira resolution.
